text:
Marc Gatcomb was signed to bring energy to Vegas's fourth line, and the hits are there: 84 in 23 games, at about 10 minutes a night. The undrafted forward from Woburn, Massachusetts, who came over from the Islanders, has delivered the physical part of the role as advertised.

The rest has been hard going. He has two points all season and none in his last 20 games, and our numbers don't call it a bad-luck drought: he had about 4.2 points' worth of expected production in that stretch, and the chances have thinned out lately too. One goal on 30 shots is low, but he isn't getting many good looks either.

The bigger concern is the five-on-five tilt. Vegas takes 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 18 points worse than when he sits, and the goals have roughly matched. That runs against last season, when Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him out there (91st percentile, over a small 494 minutes). His ice time is down about two minutes a night over his last ten. Watch whether the defensive version from Long Island comes back.
